questions.q:
The RBI issued dividend directions on 10 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The maximum dividend payout ratio was raised to 75 per cent of profit after tax from 40 per cent.
2. Extraordinary income and Level 3 unrealised gains are excluded from PAT when computing the payout.
3. The directions apply to eligible commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks and regional rural banks.
4. Foreign bank branches may remit profits even before their accounts are audited.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 reproduce the new directions. Foreign bank branches may remit profits only after audited accounts, so statement 4 is wrong. Higher payout limits let well-capitalised banks return more profit to shareholders, including the Government as an owner of public sector banks.
questions.h: Seventy-five per cent payout, up from forty.

questions.q: Under the RBI's draft framework of 6 March 2026 on limiting customer liability for fraudulent transactions up to Rs 50,000, a customer would be compensated
o: 85 per cent of net loss or Rs 25,000, whichever is lower, available once in a lifetime
the full amount of the loss up to Rs 25,000 on every occasion
50 per cent of the loss or Rs 10,000, whichever is lower, once a year
85 per cent of net loss or Rs 50,000, whichever is higher, without any limit on occasions
questions.e: The draft compensates 85 per cent of net loss subject to a cap of Rs 25,000 and only once in a lifetime. Banks must pay within five calendar days and can claim quarterly reimbursement from the RBI. Comments were invited until 6 April 2026.
questions.h: Eighty-five per cent, capped at 25,000, once.

questions.q:
The Government retained the flexible inflation target for the RBI for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
Statement-I: The inflation target for 2026-2031 stays at 4 per cent with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 per cent.
Statement-II: Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of CPI once in every five years.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Section 45ZA, inserted in 2016, requires the Centre to notify the CPI-based target every five years, which is why a fresh notification was needed for the 2026-31 block. The 4 per cent target with a 2 to 6 per cent band was carried over again from the 2021-26 block, and inflation outside the band for three consecutive quarters counts as policy failure.
questions.h: Every five years the Centre sets the CPI target.

questions.q:
On 17 March 2026 the Lok Sabha approved the second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26, and the Finance Minister introduced an Economic Stabilisation Fund. Consider the following statements:
1. The Fund has a corpus of Rs 1 lakh crore and is meant as a buffer against global shocks.
2. It sits under the reserve funds managed by the Department of Economic Affairs.
3. The Government revised the 2025-26 fiscal deficit target upward to above 4.4 per cent of GDP to fund the Fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rs 1 lakh crore Economic Stabilisation Fund is a fiscal buffer under the reserve funds managed by the DEA. The Government said the revised 2025-26 fiscal deficit target of 4.4 per cent of GDP was unchanged, so statement 3 is wrong. The net cash outgo from the supplementary demands was Rs 57,381.84 crore.
questions.h: Rs 1 lakh crore buffer, deficit target unchanged.

questions.q:
The Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendations apply to 2026-31. Consider the following statements:
1. It retained the States' share in the divisible pool of Central taxes at 41 per cent.
2. It introduced a 'contribution' criterion for horizontal devolution, measured by a State's share in aggregate GSDP.
3. It continued revenue-deficit grants to States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Commission discontinued revenue-deficit grants and recommended no State- or sector-specific grants, so statement 3 is wrong. The 41 per cent share matches the Fifteenth Commission's level, after the Fourteenth had raised it from 32 to 42 per cent. The new contribution criterion rewards States that add more to national output. Cesses and surcharges stay outside the divisible pool.
questions.h: Revenue-deficit grants were dropped.

questions.q:
India's balance-of-payments data for October-December 2025 (Q3 of 2025-26) were released in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The current account deficit was USD 13.2 billion, or 1.3 per cent of GDP.
2. Foreign exchange reserves rose during the quarter.
3. Industrial output (IIP) grew 5.3 per cent in Q3 2025-26 against 4.1 per cent a year earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CAD widened from USD 11.3 billion (1.1 per cent) a year earlier to USD 13.2 billion (1.3 per cent). Foreign exchange reserves fell by USD 24.4 billion in the quarter, so statement 2 is wrong. IIP growth at 5.3 per cent was led by manufacturing at 6.3 per cent.
questions.h: CAD 1.3 per cent; reserves fell.

questions.q:
The Union Cabinet approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA) on 18 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It is a central sector scheme with an outlay of Rs 33,660 crore to develop 100 investment-ready plug-and-play industrial parks.
2. Central support is up to Rs 1 crore per acre plus 25 per cent of project cost for external connectivity.
3. The industrial parks are chosen by nomination from the States rather than through a challenge process.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: BHAVYA runs for six years (FY2026-27 to FY2031-32) and picks projects in challenge mode, with a minimum area of 100 acres (25 acres in North-Eastern and hilly areas). It is implemented under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: BHAVYA: 100 parks, challenge mode.

questions.q: Press Note 2 of 2026, issued by DPIIT on 15 March 2026, eased the FDI regime for investors from land-border countries. Which one of the following is correct?
o: It removed the requirement that the beneficial owner be situated in a land-border country and adopted the PMLA definition of beneficial ownership, with a threshold above 10 per cent
It allowed Pakistani citizens and entities to invest under the automatic route in all sectors
It repealed Press Note 3 of 2020 completely and ended government approval for every investor
It raised the sectoral cap for defence manufacturing to 100 per cent for land-border countries
questions.e: The press note relaxes Press Note 3 (2020), which mainly affected Chinese investment, by moving to the beneficial-ownership test used under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Pakistani citizens and entities still need government approval and are barred from sectors such as defence and atomic energy.
questions.h: Beneficial owner now means above 10 per cent.

questions.q:
On 23 March 2026 the Government fully restored RoDTEP benefits to exporters.
Statement-I: The 50 per cent cap on RoDTEP remission rates, introduced in February 2026, was removed.
Statement-II: RoDTEP, launched in 2021, replaced the Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS).
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The cap was lifted because the West Asia conflict disrupted logistics for exporters. RoDTEP did replace MEIS in 2021, but that history does not explain why the cap was removed, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. RoDTEP covers over 8,500 tariff lines with rebates of 0.5 to 4.3 per cent of FOB value.
questions.h: Cap removed because of logistics disruption.

questions.q: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry launched the Rs 497 crore RELIEF scheme (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) on 16 March 2026. The scheme provides
o: interest subvention of 3 per cent on all pre-shipment export credit for two years
credit-insurance support through ECGC to exporters hit by the West Asia crisis, with new cover for 16 March to 15 June 2026
a freight subsidy on every container leaving Indian ports
direct cash grants to exporters for all lost cargo
questions.e: RELIEF extends new ECGC credit-insurance cover for exports to 10 West Asian countries, with up to Rs 50 lakh cover per MSME exporter without prior insurance. India is also exploring a domestic Protection and Indemnity club because of Strait of Hormuz risks.
questions.h: RELIEF means insurance cover through ECGC.

questions.q:
The Ministry of Mines notified the Mineral (Auction) Second Amendment Rules, 2026 on 30 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The auction premium was removed for certain critical minerals that form less than 10 per cent of the block value, other than graphite, phosphate and potash.
2. States must decide mineral-inclusion applications within 60 days.
3. The draft Mineral Exchange Rules, 2026 propose the Geological Survey of India as regulator of mineral exchanges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The amendments waive the auction premium on minor-share critical minerals except graphite, phosphate and potash, and set a 60-day limit for States on inclusion applications. The draft Mineral Exchange Rules of 19 March propose the Indian Bureau of Mines, not the GSI, as regulator.
questions.h: Indian Bureau of Mines would regulate exchanges.

questions.q:
The Prime Minister inaugurated India's first semiconductor Assembly, Test, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) facility at Sanand, Gujarat, run by Micron Technology. Consider the following statements:
1. It has started India's first commercial semiconductor chip production.
2. ATMP covers the back-end steps of assembling, testing, marking and packaging chips.
3. The plant fabricates silicon wafers from raw material.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ATMP is back-end work on finished wafers, not wafer fabrication, so statement 3 is wrong. The Sanand plant marks the start of India's first commercial chip production and strengthens the country's place in the global semiconductor value chain.
questions.h: ATMP is back-end, not wafer fabrication.

questions.q:
The Union Cabinet on 25 March 2026 approved the Regional Connectivity Scheme - Modified UDAN. Consider the following statements:
1. The outlay is Rs 28,840 crore over ten years, FY2026-27 to FY2035-36.
2. It includes 100 new airports from unserved airstrips and 200 helipads.
3. Operation and maintenance support is capped at Rs 30.6 crore per airport per year for three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Modified UDAN is a ten-year scheme to develop 100 new airports from unserved airstrips and 200 helipads, with Viability Gap Funding of Rs 10,043 crore. The O&M cap is Rs 3.06 crore, not Rs 30.6 crore, per airport per year for three years.
questions.h: Modified UDAN: 100 airports, 200 helipads.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved a Small Hydro Power (SHP) Development Scheme for FY2026-27 to FY2030-31 on 18 March 2026. Which one of the following is correct?
o: The scheme covers projects of 25 MW to 100 MW capacity
Central assistance is 50 per cent of project cost in all hilly States
Central assistance is 30 per cent of cost (up to Rs 30 crore per project) in the North-East and international border districts, and 20 per cent (up to Rs 20 crore) elsewhere
Imported turbines and equipment are encouraged under the scheme
questions.e: The scheme, with an outlay of about Rs 2,585 crore, targets about 1,500 MW from projects of 1 to 25 MW and insists on indigenous equipment. Small hydro is administered by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and is expected to draw about Rs 15,000 crore of investment.
questions.h: Thirty per cent in NE and border, twenty elsewhere.

questions.q:
In March 2026 India invoked the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to direct refiners to maximise LPG production and prioritise domestic households. Consider the following statements:
1. The Centre directed refiners to prioritise households over industry and petrochemicals.
2. India imports about 60 per cent of its LPG demand.
3. Section 3 of the Act empowers the Centre to regulate the production, supply and distribution of essential commodities.
4. The 2020 amendment permanently bars stock limits on cereals, pulses, potatoes, onions and oilseeds.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are accurate. The 2020 amendment allows control over cereals, pulses, potatoes, onions and oilseeds only in extraordinary circumstances such as steep price rises or war, not a permanent bar. The invocation followed disruption of supplies from the Gulf.
questions.h: Extraordinary circumstances only for foodgrain stock limits.

questions.q:
In March 2026 the Centre cut the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED) on petrol and diesel and raised export duties on diesel and ATF.
Statement-I: The Centre raised export duties on diesel and ATF to cut the under-recoveries of oil marketing companies.
Statement-II: Disruption of Gulf oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent crude above USD 111 per barrel.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: With Brent above USD 111 a barrel, domestic prices could not rise in step, so oil marketing companies IOCL, BPCL and HPCL faced under-recoveries. Cutting SAED and taxing diesel and ATF exports kept more fuel at home and eased the losses. Statement-II therefore explains Statement-I.
questions.h: Costly crude, fuel kept at home.

questions.q:
The Ministry of Heavy Industries revised the PM E-DRIVE scheme in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. Subsidies for electric two-wheelers were extended until 31 July 2026.
2. Subsidies for electric three-wheelers (rickshaws and carts) were extended until 31 March 2028.
3. The scheme is administered by the Ministry of Power.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The scheme, approved in October 2024 with an outlay of Rs 10,900 crore, plans 72,300 public fast chargers and is run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries. BHEL will build an EV 'Super App'. Hence statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: E-2W till July 2026; e-3W till March 2028.

questions.q:
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy introduced List-III of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM). Consider the following statements:
1. List-III covers solar ingots and wafers.
2. It takes effect on 1 June 2028.
3. It is issued by the Ministry of Power.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ALMM lists are issued by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, not the Ministry of Power, so statement 3 is wrong. List-III follows the earlier lists for solar modules and cells and pushes domestic manufacturing upstream to ingots and wafers from 1 June 2028.
questions.h: MNRE issues ALMM, not Power.

questions.q: The Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs (MCGS-MSME) was modified in March 2026. Which one of the following is a feature of the modified scheme?
o: The scheme is limited to manufacturing MSMEs and the machinery share remains 75 per cent
The guarantee cover applies to loans up to Rs 5 crore with a 90 per cent guarantee
The scheme is run by SIDBI as the sole guarantor
Service-sector MSMEs became eligible and the minimum share of machinery and equipment in project cost fell to 60 per cent from 75 per cent
questions.e: The National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC) guarantees 60 per cent of loans up to Rs 100 crore, for 10 years, and the scheme covers loans sanctioned over four years or until Rs 7 lakh crore of cumulative guarantees. The modification follows the Union Budget 2025-26 announcement.
questions.h: Services in; machinery share 75 to 60.

questions.q: The Department of Financial Services directed banks to use the Grameen Credit Score as the default tool for assessing rural borrowers, especially first-time borrowers. The Grameen Credit Score is
o: a 300-900 score developed by credit information companies, drawing in Phase I on data such as Kisan Credit Cards, SVAMITVA, priority sector loans and tractor loans
a 0-100 score developed by NABARD from MGNREGA wage records alone
a 1-10 rating issued by the Reserve Bank of India for cooperative banks
a CIBIL-only score valid only for urban borrowers
questions.e: Announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, the score uses alternative data to assess people with thin credit histories. It follows the usual 300-900 credit-score scale used by credit information companies.
questions.h: Rural borrowers get a 300-900 score.

questions.q:
A Parliamentary panel's recommendations on Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were reported in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The panel recommended privatising all RRBs.
2. Under the One State-One RRB policy, the number of RRBs fell from a peak of 196 to 28.
3. RRBs are owned by the Centre (50 per cent), the sponsor bank (35 per cent) and the State Government (15 per cent).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The panel recommended IPOs for profitable RRBs, not privatisation. RRBs earned a consolidated net profit of Rs 7,720 crore in the first nine months of FY2025-26 with gross NPAs at a 13-year low of 5.4 per cent. Ownership at 50:35:15 is set by the RRB Act, 1976.
questions.h: RRBs: 50, 35, 15; IPO, not privatisation.

questions.q: On 23 March 2026 the SEBI Board adopted the recommendations of its High-Level Committee on conflicts of interest. Which of the following was among them?
o: Banning SEBI officials from holding any bank deposits during their tenure
Requiring only the Chairman to disclose holdings once at the time of appointment

Treating the Chairman and Whole-Time Members as 'insiders', requiring their equity holdings to be liquidated, frozen or sold on joining, and capping investment in any one intermediary's products at 25 per cent of the official's financial portfolio
Allowing free trading in listed shares by Whole-Time Members after prior intimation
questions.e: The rules are meant to remove any suspicion of misuse of unpublished price-sensitive information. Limits extend prospectively to spouses and dependent family members, with initial, annual and event-based disclosures.
questions.h: Regulator officials are insiders.

questions.q:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released a new series of national accounts in the 2026 cycle. Consider the following statements:
1. The new base year is 2022-23, replacing 2011-12.
2. Double deflation replaces single deflation in manufacturing and agriculture.
3. The series was released by NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MoSPI, not NITI Aayog, compiles national accounts. The 2022-23 base was chosen as the first 'normal' year after the Covid disruption, and the series draws on GST, e-Vahan and PFMS data. Shankar IAS notes that GDP at current prices comes out about 3 to 4 per cent smaller than under the 2011-12 series.
questions.h: New base 2022-23; double deflation.

questions.q:
The results of the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) 2025, covering January to December 2025, were released. Consider the following statements:
1. It is conducted by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI.
2. It covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises in manufacturing, trade and services.
3. It covers the agricultural holdings of farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ASUSE excludes agriculture; it tracks employment, gross value added, wages and digital use in unincorporated non-agricultural firms, so statement 3 is wrong. Its results are an input to GDP estimation and the national accounts.
questions.h: Non-agricultural firms only.

questions.q: The growth of the Index of Eight Core Industries slowed to 2.3 per cent in February 2026 from 4.7 per cent in January. Which one of the following is NOT among the eight core industries?
questions.e: The eight core industries are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement and electricity. Iron ore is an input for steel and is not itself in the index. Together they account for 40.27 per cent of the weight of items in the Index of Industrial Production.
questions.h: Eight core: coal to electricity; iron ore absent.
